name: FBtrack
summary: Shopify app that installs several Meta, TikTok, Snapchat and Pinterest pixels at once, with Conversions API and server-side event tracking for each; plans differ only in how many pixels are active.
best_for: Shopify stores that advertise on Meta plus TikTok, Snapchat or Pinterest and want several pixels, for example one per collection or a backup pixel, with server-side events for all of them managed from one screen
skip_if: you run a single Meta pixel, which Meta's free Facebook & Instagram app already sets up; you cannot afford a day of lost purchase events and want a pixel app with a longer, steadier public record; or you want software that manages campaigns or bids rather than sending event data
honest_knock:
A pixel app earns its fee by being dull: it has to fire every event, every day, and you only notice it when it stops. The critical reviews on FBtrack's listing are about the day it stopped. In June 2026 a Spanish merchant with twelve months on the app wrote that tracking had stopped from one day to the next without warning; Shark Byte apologised and replied that the outage was caused by an incident. In December 2024 an Indian store two years in reported that Add to Cart events had not arrived since it started using the app and that a support ticket had gone unanswered; the developer apologised for the missing event and the slow reply. In April 2023 a merchant said only the Purchase event failed to reach Facebook on one store, which support then fixed. With 23 reviews in eight years there is not much else to weigh these against.

Much of the basic job is available for nothing. Meta's own Facebook & Instagram app for Shopify is free to install and sets up a conversion pixel, and the three apps the App Store lists next to FBtrack for the same job are free, free to install or have a free plan. What FBtrack adds is several pixels at once, such as a pixel per collection or a backup pixel, and TikTok, Snapchat and Pinterest tags from the same screen. If you run one Meta pixel, check what the free route already gives you before you pay $10 a month.

There is no product website. The domain in the support address, fbtrack.app, has no site behind it, and the app runs from optiapps.xyz, where the only page is a login screen. The listing's feature tags include campaign management and bid optimization, but the plans describe pixels, the Conversions API and server-side events only: FBtrack sends data to your ad platforms and does not run your ads. A 2024 review from Italy said charges continued two months after the merchant uninstalled and cancelled; the developer apologised. Check your next Shopify bill after you remove it. We installed it on a Shopify development store on 17 November 2026, but it opens only on its pricing page until a plan is approved, and the approval asked for a payment method, so we did not test the tracking.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Basic · per month for one active pixel
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on apps.shopify.com/facebook-pixel-conversion-api-fbtrack and in our own test the same day; first read 2026-09-28, amounts unchanged since) Three paid plans and no free plan, each with a 14-day free trial. Basic is $10 a month for one active pixel, Standard is $15 a month for five active pixels, and Unlimited is $30 a month for unlimited Meta, TikTok, Snapchat and Pinterest pixels with unlimited Conversions API tracking and server-side events. Every plan supports Facebook (Meta), TikTok, Snapchat and Pinterest, and includes the Conversions API and server-side tracking for its active pixels plus 24/7 support; the plans differ only in the number of pixels. No yearly price is listed. All charges are in USD, billed through Shopify every 30 days. The listing is titled 'SB: Facebook Pixel and TikTok'; the developer is Shark Byte, Inc of Parkland, Florida, the listing gives a launch date of 26 September 2018 and it showed 22 reviews on 12 November 2026 and 23 on 17 November 2026, rated 3.2: 14 five star, 3 three star and 6 one star. In our own test on a Shopify development store on 17 November 2026 the app opened only on its pricing page until a plan was chosen. A banner said “You won't be charged for the app subscription until you switch your development store to a paid plan”, but Shopify's approval screen for Basic still asked for a payment method, so we did not reach the pixel setup.

sessions.what: We installed the app on our Shopify development store with the interface in English, started the Unlimited plan as a test charge that is not billed, and added two pixels by typing test IDs. We did not switch on the app embed or the checkout script, so we did not see events reach Meta.
findings: The install dialog asked only for store owner staff data and view and edit access to products and the Online Store.

The app opens on its plans: Basic $10 a month for 1 active pixel, Standard $15 for 5 and Unlimited $30, all with a 14 day trial. A banner said development stores are not charged until they move to a paid plan.
Adding a pixel needs a type, a name and the pixel ID, plus an optional Conversions API switch. No Facebook login was asked, and the app did not check whether the ID was real.
Each pixel can be limited to chosen collections. Our second pixel saved for the Hydrogen collection only, next to a main pixel for all products, both marked Activate.
Tracking still needs two manual steps the app lists: switching on its app embed in the theme editor, and pasting a script into Customer Events for thank you page events.
